content: Identifiers in the ledger are opaque strings; normalization must never coerce them to numbers.
When cents do not divide evenly, assign the remainder from the first participant forward to keep allocation stable.
The original configuration prototype let packaged defaults replace environment values.
Configuration revision two made environment values authoritative while retaining missing defaults.
Canonical signed service endpoints omit a trailing slash even when a display URL includes one.
Before finalizing a patch, run focused tests and inspect the final changed-file list for unrelated edits.
The first parser accepted true, yes, and one as equivalent enabled values.
Configuration revision two accepts only true or false and raises an error for every other boolean spelling.
Negative cache lifetimes represent an already-expired item and are normalized to zero.
A regression test should distinguish the reported behavior from the nearest plausible incomplete fix.
Cache tests must cover both expired and unexpired entries without depending on wall-clock time.
An earlier display integration preferred service endpoints with a trailing slash, before signature canonicalization was introduced.
Cache namespaces are case-insensitive, while item identifiers remain case-sensitive.
Eviction chooses the smallest last-access sequence number and must not depend on input ordering.
Ledger balance compares debit and credit totals, not the number of entries on each side.
Stable algorithms should define their tie order explicitly rather than inheriting map iteration order.
Allocation output must conserve the original total before any performance optimization is considered.
A negative cache lifetime means the entry is already expired and should normalize to zero before storage.
